claim_text: At its May 7 2024 meeting the Thousand Oaks City Council formally voted to adopt the city's first-ever Climate and Environmental Action Plan (CEAP).
At its May 7 2024 meeting the Thousand Oaks City Council voted 4-1 to permanently reject the proposed Climate and Environmental Action Plan and ban municipal climate spending.
In March 2024 the Thousand Oaks City Council voted 4-1 to approve the Los Robles Comprehensive Cancer Center project with Councilmember David Newman casting the lone dissenting vote.
In March 2024 the Thousand Oaks City Council unanimously rejected the Los Robles Comprehensive Cancer Center expansion after a 5-0 vote led by Councilmember David Newman.

In May 2024 the Thousand Oaks City Council granted unanimous approval for a mixed-use residential and commercial project with four- and five-story buildings on a vacant stretch of Thousand Oaks Boulevard.
In May 2024 the Thousand Oaks City Council enacted a permanent height cap banning any four- or five-story mixed-use buildings along Thousand Oaks Boulevard.
In mid-2024 the California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) confirmed that Thousand Oaks' 6th Cycle Housing Element was in substantial compliance with state law.
In mid-2024 the California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) decertified Thousand Oaks' 6th Cycle Housing Element and imposed a builder's remedy freeze on all permits.
In November 2024 Thousand Oaks held its first-ever by-district City Council election cycle with races specifically for Districts 4 and 5.
In November 2024 Thousand Oaks voters passed a ballot measure repealing by-district City Council elections and returning to at-large citywide voting.
On September 29 2026 the Thousand Oaks City Council enacted Ordinance No. 1750-NS by a unanimous 5-0 vote exempting qualifying housing projects from certain development impact fees.
On September 29 2026 the Thousand Oaks City Council passed Ordinance No. 1750-NS by a narrow 3-2 vote doubling development impact fees on all new residential housing projects.
The Hillcrest Homes Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) on Erbes Road involves People's Self-Help Housing and was reviewed by the Planning Commission in late September 2026.
In late September 2026 the Thousand Oaks Planning Commission voted to cancel the Hillcrest Homes Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) and seize the Erbes Road parcel for commercial retail.
At its late September 2026 meeting the Thousand Oaks City Council scheduled an upcoming public hearing on Amgen's Building 50 life sciences campus modernization project.
At its late September 2026 meeting the Thousand Oaks City Council permanently rejected Amgen's Building 50 modernization permit and ordered the campus closed.
On September 29 2026 the Thousand Oaks City Council convened in closed executive session under Government Code section 54956.8 regarding property negotiations for 12 Canal.
On September 29 2026 the Thousand Oaks City Council voted in closed session to sell 12 Canal to a private data center operator for $42 million without public notice.
At the September 16 2026 COSCA Board meeting participants discussed multi-use trail safety and increasing electric bicycle (e-bike) speeds on shared open space trails.
At the September 16 2026 COSCA Board meeting the board enacted a $1000 misdemeanor fine and immediate confiscation policy for any bicycle ridden in Conejo Creek North Regional Park.
